answer: In an autonomous AI economy, a cryptographic trust prism can defend against Sybil attacks by anchoring identity verification to verifiable computational resource allocation. Much like planting a digital orchard where every legitimate agent requires a dedicated physical node and staked cryptographic proof to bear fruit, unauthorized entities are starved from the secure garden of the consensus network. An attacker attempting to flood the system faces prohibitive computational expenditure and capital lock-up costs, making mass identity fabrication economically irrational.
